children: Government bond supply will be very low in the eurozone this week, with only Slovakia, Germany and Finland auctioning bonds. Up to a combined 3 billion euros in offer volumes marks the lowest weekly supply year to date, Commerzbank's Rainer Guntermann says in a note. Slovakia kicks off this week's auctions with an indicative offer volume of 500 million euros for bonds maturing in 2029, 2036, 2037 and 2051 on Monday. On Tuesday, Germany will auction 1 billion euros in 2029- and 2053-dated green bonds, while Finland will offer up to 1.5 billion euros in 2031- and 2036-dated bonds. Accompanying the institutional supply, Italy will open subsriptions for retail bonds on Monday, running through Friday. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
